g.text: Rendered evidence from captured output

teps 2 and 4 into one versioned object so every
client reads a run the same way. Four things to know before gating on it:

* **
`measurementUnit` ships with every count.** Under per-case grading the\n counts are case-execution *variants*, with iterations as
trials inside them;\n under a suite-wide accuracy threshold they are trials. The same suite reports\n a different total under e
ach — 3 against 15 for three cases run five times —\n so a count without its unit is not a fact, and a rate is never converted\n
across that line.\n* **It explains the verdict; it never re-decides it.** The run's own decision is\n the authority and is carri
ed through on `decision`. The per-trial\n `diagnostics` sit underneath it — a case can pass with a failing trial in it,\n so tal
lying diagnostics gives a different answer than the platform reached.\n* **`verdict: \"notEstablished\"` is not a failure and not
`inconclusive`.** It\n means no verdict exists at all (unfinished, stopped early, or undecidable);\n `undecided.reason` says whi
ch. `inconclusive` *is* a decision — the validity\n phase ran and withheld a verdict.\n* **`diagnostics.complete` says whether yo
u have the whole list.** A page\n fetched with a `cursor` is never complete, and `scannedIterations` separates\n \"nothing faile

d" from "we did not look".

Evidence is scoped to the claim it supports: for a measured failure the span
ids, prompt indexes
and reasons come from the first failed stage's row alone,\nand `evidence.tracePath` is an API-relative path you can append to you

r base URL
to read the full trace.

`model` takes an id from the hosted catalog — `provider/name` form, e.g.
`anthropic/claude
-haiku-4.5` — and runs on your organization's credits.\nProvider-native ids (e.g. `claude-sonnet-4-5`) are bring-your-own-key: pas
s\nthe key in `modelApiKeys`. A model the API can't execute is rejected at\ncreate time with `VALIDATION_ERROR`; `details.hostedMo

dels` lists the valid
hosted ids for that provider.

Reruns are even shorter: `{ "suiteId": "..." }` reruns the suite exact
ly as\nconfigured, connecting the suite's saved server selection (the `202` response\nlists the resolved `servers`). Pass `serverI
ds` to override the selection; a\nsuite with no saved selection requires it (`VALIDATION_ERROR` with\n`details.reason: \"NO_SAVED_

SERVER_SELECTION"` otherwise).

### Running against a project environment

A [project environment](#endpoints) is launchable
only through a suite that has\nit **attached**. Attach them first with\n`PATCH /projects/{projectId}/eval-suites/{suiteId}` and an
`environmentIds`\narray (send `null` to detach them all; `[]` is rejected — use `null`), then\npass `environmentId` on the run. I
t must be one of that suite's attached\nenvironments; anything else is a `400` with\n`details.reason: \"ENVIRONMENT_NOT_ATTACHED\"

`, raised before any case is
authored or any server connected.

Omitting `environmentId` is meaningful, and depends on the suit
ronment is used automatically. The `202`\n response's `environment` field says so;\n* **several** attached → `400` with `details.

reason: "ENVIRONMENT_REQUIRED"`,
 naming the candidates.

The environment supplies the closed server set — including the ser
vers its\npinned plugin versions contribute — so `serverIds` is not required and is\n**rejected** alongside it (`400`), rather tha
n accepted and ignored: honoring\nboth would connect a different set than the run is stamped with. The same goes\nfor a `serverIds

` override on an environment-based suite
(`details.reason: "ENVIRONMENT_SERVERS_NOT_OVERRIDABLE"`).

The run is pinned to the
environment revision resolved at launch: if the\nenvironment changes in between, the run is rejected with `CONFLICT` (409)\nrathe
r than executing against a different configuration than the one whose\ntools were captured. Use\n`GET /projects/{projectId}/enviro

nments/{environmentId}/resolve` to see what it
will connect before launching.

When creating a new inline suite, `POST .../eval
-runs` also accepts `hosts: [{ host: \"Claude\", servers: [\"my-server\"] }]`, using the same host name or ID and optional server
selection as `POST .../eval-suites`. A single host is selected for the run automatically. With multiple attachments, use `namedHos
tId` to select the run's client. For an existing suite, update its attachments first. If `hosts` is omitted, the backend supplies
the project's default client.\n\nRun reads and listings expose `client: { id, name, source, hostStyle?, modelId? }` when recorded.
`id` is the named host ID or `null`; `source` is `environment`, `attached_host`, `suite_default`, or `sdk`. The name is durable e
ven if the host is deleted. SDK executions use `SDK harness`; `launcher.client` separately identifies the launching process. Older
runs without a descriptor omit `client`. `modelSource: \"case\"` means the run's sole model came from its case snapshot; `client_
default` and `override` retain their existing meanings.\n\nEvery run records which environment it used. `GET .../eval-runs/{runId}
` (and\nthe run listings) return `environment: { id, name, revision }` — read from the\nrun's immutable snapshot, not the suite's

current attachments — or `null` for a
run that used a saved server selection.

Per-organization
concurrency is capped (default
**2** concurrent runs); exceeding it returns\n`429` with `details.reason: \"CONCURRENT_RUN_LIMIT\"` — wait for an active run\nto

finish.

If a server answers `401 OAUTH_REQUIRED`, complete the OAuth flow yourself
(the SDK's `runOAuthLogin` handles interact
ive, headless, and\nclient-credentials flows) and upload the token to one of the server's\n[accounts](#server-accounts). Subsequen

t runs inject the stored token, and
refresh it server-side when you stored a refresh token.

## Reasoning effort

A reasoning
effort is a **saved setting on a model selection**, not a free-standing\nfield. A `ModelSelection` (`modelId`, `source`, an optio
nal `connectionRef`, and a\n`fallback`) carries it as `settings.reasoningEffort`, and the same shape is\naccepted everywhere a mod

el choice is saved:

| Where | Field |
| - | - |
| Client (`PATCH /projects/{projectId}/clients/{client}`) | `set.modelSelecti
on` (or `config.modelSelection` on a whole-config replacement) |\n| Project environment (`POST`, `PATCH`, `POST .../ensure-adhoc`)
| `modelSelection`, read back on the environment |\n| Eval case (`POST`, `PATCH .../cases`) | `models[].selection`, read back on
the case |\n| Eval suite (`PATCH /projects/{projectId}/eval-suites/{suiteId}`) | `executionConfig.modelSelection`, read back on th
** `none`, `minimal`, `low`, `medium`, `high`, `xhigh`, `max`. Which of\n them a model accepts is `supportedReasoningEfforts` on
each row of the public\n `GET /v1/models` catalog. An empty or absent list means no effort is offered for\n that model — do not
guess one.\n* **Applied or refused, never dropped.** A saved effort is applied by the route\n the run takes and recorded on the e

xecution record, or refused with
 `capability_missing` before any spend. An effort replaces the sampling
 temperature.
* **A
selection belongs to one model.** It must be for the `model` / `modelId` it\n sits beside (`400` otherwise); sent alone it pins i

ts own model. A bare model
 change on a suite or environment drops a selection saved for the old model
 instead of failing.
*
**Cases keep their selections.** A `models` PATCH replaces the array, but an\n entry that omits `selection` keeps the case's exi
sting selection for that\n model. Send `selection: null` to drop it.\n* **Clearing.** `null` clears a saved selection on a client
`set`, an environment\n or a suite, keeping the bare model id.\n* **Never a secret.** A selection has no credential field; an un

known key
 (`apiKey`, …) is a `400`.
* **Environments need the capability.** `GET .../environments/capabilities`
 reports `mo
delSelections`; an older deployment rejects the field.\n* **`advancedConfig.reasoningEffort` is retired.** It was never applied, s
